ordered_diagnoses: Renal cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome

s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a large renal mass and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms
Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression on thorax CT
Invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on radiologically guided biopsy of renal mass

shortlist: Renal cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the sudden onset of oral and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Renal cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Explains the large renal mass and associated skin lesions

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma with cutaneous metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the invasive carcinoma and cutaneous findings

shortlist.label: Bazex syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Associates with skin lesions and internal malignancies, including renal cancer

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the oral lesions and association with a large renal mass

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden onset of oral lesions, extensive papillomatosis, and characteristic palm lesions are consistent with florid cutaneous papillomatosis, a rare paraneoplastic syndrome associated with internal malignancies, in this case, the urothelial carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation

rejected.label: Renal cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome
rejected.why: The biopsy revealed urothelial carcinoma, not renal cell carcinoma

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma with cutaneous metastasis
rejected.why: The skin lesions are more consistent with a paraneoplastic syndrome rather than direct metastasis

rejected.label: Bazex syndrome
rejected.why: Bazex syndrome typically presents with acral lesions and is associated with squamous cell carcinoma, not urothelial carcinoma

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathology do not support paraneoplastic pemphigus, which typically involves autoantibodies against skin and mucous membranes
